questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Side road.
Merge.
Yield the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Side road.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a side road is ahead.

questions.question: You are driving on the freeway behind a large truck. How should you drive?

options.text: Drive close behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.
Stay farther back from the truck than you would from a regular car.
Stay one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back from the truck than you would from a regular car.
questions.explanation: If you drive too close to a truck, the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. Staying too close is dangerous because you need time to stop if the truck brakes suddenly.

questions.question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:

options.text: Press hard on the accelerator.
Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
Set the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors for traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors to see traffic around you before you stop. Then release the accelerator and move your foot to the brake. Press the brake smoothly and steadily to stop.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns drivers that bicycles may be crossing the road ahead.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only use the rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Only use the left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes. Check multiple times if needed. Watch traffic ahead and in the lane next to you.

questions.question: When driving in work zones, you should:

options.text: Follow the driver in front of you closely.
Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from barriers, trucks, equipment, workers, and other vehicles. Increase your following distance and never tailgate.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 pounds are allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings and alert you to immediate conditions. This sign warns that a steep hill is ahead. Slow down and shift to a lower gear to control your speed and protect your brakes.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines down the center of the road mean passing is:

options.text: Allowed from both directions.
Allowed only from your direction of travel.
Not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean traffic moves in opposite directions. Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.question: If your vehicle loses traction on wet roads, you should:

options.text: Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.
Apply the brakes firmly to prevent sliding.
Slow down gradually without using the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without using the brakes.
questions.explanation: In heavy rain, your tires may ride on a layer of water and lose contact with the road. This is called hydroplaning. If this happens, slow down gradually and do not apply the brakes.

questions.question: You should leave extra space when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A passenger vehicle.
A motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles stop faster than other vehicles. You need room to stop if the rider brakes or falls. Also, motorcycles are hard to see at night because they have only one tail light.

questions.question: Which of the following is dangerous in work zones?

options.text: Driving too close to another vehicle
Not watching for workers and moving equipment
Both of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above
questions.explanation: In work zones, slow down for traffic conditions and do not follow other vehicles too closely. Watch carefully for workers and machines.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should NOT:

options.text: Continue on the freeway and find another route.
Go to the next exit, leave the freeway, and return to your proper exit.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on the road or shoulder. Continue to the next exit or crossroad. Other drivers do not expect vehicles backing up, which can cause crashes.

questions.question: Pressing the brakes hard on ice and snow often:

options.text: Helps you stop faster.
Locks the front wheels, making you lose steering control.
Keeps the brakes from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Locks the front wheels, making you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock the front wheels and cause you to lose steering. Drive at a safe speed for the conditions to avoid hard braking.

questions.question: If you become drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Try to stay awake.
Stop and take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired, stop at the nearest rest stop to take a nap, stretch, or change drivers. Caffeine pills are not a safe replacement for rest and can make driving more dangerous.

questions.question: Temporary signs in construction and maintenance work areas have:

options.text: A red background with green writing.
An orange background with black writing.
A yellow background with blue writing.

questions.correctAnswerText: An orange background with black writing.
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: When an officer directs traffic at an active traffic light, drivers should:

options.text: Follow the traffic light.
Follow the officer's directions.
Honk at the officer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the officer's directions.
questions.explanation: Traffic signals control traffic at intersections. When an officer is directing traffic, follow the officer's directions instead of the signal.

questions.question: Who must wear a safety belt in a moving vehicle?

options.text: Only the driver
Only children
Everyone in the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Everyone in the vehicle
questions.explanation: All vehicle occupants, including the driver, must wear a safety belt. Children must use proper child-restraint systems. The driver is responsible for making sure everyone follows this law.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You must travel through the intersection at the posted speed limit.
The maximum speed is 55 mph under normal conditions.
You must not drive slower than the posted speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum speed is 55 mph under normal conditions.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the maximum speed allowed on that road. You may drive slower based on road conditions, but you cannot drive faster than the posted limit.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you may:

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing and checking traffic.
Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after stopping completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means stop. You must remain stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, you must:

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends.
Get ready for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and keep your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs warn you of workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: If the road is wet or icy, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Drive at the posted speed.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Wet, snowy, or icy roads reduce tire grip. You should slow down to stay safe.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a construction zone?

options.text: Stop to watch the workers.
Drive closer to the car in front of you.
Pass carefully and keep your eyes on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass carefully and keep your eyes on the road.
questions.explanation: Do not slow down to look at things happening in the construction zone. Keep moving and focus on driving to avoid traffic problems.

questions.question: What are blind spots?

options.text: Areas where you lose your vision when tired.
Areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
Traffic control devices.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas near the rear corners of your vehicle that your mirrors cannot show. Look over your shoulder to check these areas before changing lanes.

questions.question: A car suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve to another lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a car merges too close in front of you, release the gas pedal. This creates space without hard braking or swerving.

questions.question: What do broken yellow lines mean?

options.text: No passing allowed.
Separate lanes moving in the same direction.
Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Separate lanes moving in opposite directions.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Broken lines mean passing is allowed when safe.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with flashing red lights, you should:

options.text: Drive faster than the train.
Stop completely.
Find a way around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely.
questions.explanation: Always obey railroad crossing signs and lights. Never try to drive around barriers.

questions.question: What is the main idea behind defensive driving?

options.text: Other drivers will always do the right thing.
Expect what other drivers might do and be ready to react.
Don't expect anything good from other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Expect what other drivers might do and be ready to react.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means guessing what mistakes other drivers might make and preparing to respond safely.

questions.question: As you drive faster, what becomes more important?

options.text: Turn on your headlights.
Look far ahead of your vehicle.
Change lanes often.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look far ahead of your vehicle.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds mean longer stopping distances. Look far ahead to give yourself time to react safely to dangers.

questions.question: You are in a minor crash with no injuries. What should you do?

options.text: Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane.
Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
Never move your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if you can.
questions.explanation: After a crash with no injuries, move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means go. Turn in the direction of the arrow after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.
